newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT-Dollar in test of top of the range.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Dollar in test of top of the range.

text.p: Buoyed by good gains on Friday, the dollar is likely to try and test the top of its current range -- but remains vulnerable to a setback from loftier levels, analysts said.
"We are still in that 1.5290/1.5730 (-mark) range," said Scott Siller, senior analyst at MCM CurrencyWatch. "I'm not getting any signal telling me we'll get a breakout there."
After giving signs of weakness late Thursday, the dollar managed to hold above key support in the 1.5340/50-mark area and marched on to stop just short of testing resistance at 1.5555 marks.

Technicians agreed the dollar's ability to hold the 1.5340/50-mark level earlier this week -- and despite the turmoil in the stock and bond markets -- was a bullish signal, but one that needed confirmation.
"We tested this morning a rising support line of the almost two-week consolidation at 1.5375 marks," Siller said.
Dollar/yen is sending even stronger signs of improvement, ending the week just shy of 114.00, an important level in terms of market psychology.
But the real technical test awaits the dollar at 114.70/75 -- the high on December 2.
"A break above 114.70, a rising trend suport, would be a bullish breakout," Siller pointed out.
As for the dollar/Swiss rate, Siller said it was the "most confusing of them all because it is improving much faster than dollar/mark."
Though some fresh bearishness cannot be ruled out for dollar/Swiss under 1.3300, it is gathering momentum to attack threee solid resistance levels in a row -- 1.3305, 1.3330 and 1.3360.
"If we break above that (1.3300), it would set the tone for a dollar rally," Siller also said.
On the crosses, mark/Swiss which made a 1996 high on Wednesday, may well be the rate to watch for volatility next week, analysts said.
